title: Filter by Grade
description: Write a query to get all students who are in the 'Freshman' grade.
explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows based on a condition. Only rows where grade equals 'Freshman' will be returned.

title: Filter by Age
description: Write a query to get students who are older than 20 years old.
explanation: The > operator selects values greater than the specified number.

title: AND Operator
description: Which query gets students who are Freshmen AND older than 20?
hints: AND requires both conditions to be true
explanation: The AND operator requires all conditions to be true for a row to be included.

options.text: SELECT * FROM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman' AND age > 20;
SELECT * FROM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman' OR age > 20;
SELECT * FROM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman' OR age > 20;
SELECT * FROM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman' AND age < 20;

title: Multiple Conditions
description: Write a query to get students who are in grade 'Senior' OR older than 21.
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students WHERE grade = 'Senior' OR age > 21;
explanation: The OR operator returns rows where at least one condition is true.

title: IN Operator
description: Write a query to get students whose grade is either 'Freshman' or 'Senior'.
hints: Use IN to check multiple values
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students WHERE grade IN ('Freshman', 'Senior');
explanation: The IN operator allows you to specify multiple values in a WHERE clause.

title: LIKE Pattern Match
description: Write a query to get all teachers whose department starts with 'C'.
hints: 'C%' matches any string starting with C
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM teachers WHERE department LIKE 'C%';
explanation: The LIKE operator with % wildcard matches any sequence of characters.

title: Fix WHERE Clause
description: This query has an error. Fix it: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age = 'twenty';
hints: Age is a number, not a string
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age = 20;
explanation: Numeric values should not be enclosed in quotes. Use = 20 instead of = 'twenty'.
brokenQuery: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age = 'twenty';

title: Combined Conditions
description: Write a query to get students who are Freshmen OR Sophomores, but only if they are older than 19.
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students WHERE (grade = 'Freshman' OR grade = 'Sophomore') AND age > 19;
explanation: Parentheses control the order of evaluation. The OR condition is evaluated first, then AND with age.

title: Complete the WHERE Clause
description: Complete the query to get teachers from the Math department: SELECT * FROM teachers WHERE department ___ 'Math';
hints: The operator goes between column and value
explanation: The = operator checks for equality between the column value and the specified string.

title: Predict Filter Results
description: What will this query return? SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students WHERE grade = 'Senior';
explanation: This query counts the number of students in the Senior grade. There are 2 seniors in the data.
